ai.summary: Evalbuff restructured around two modes: Commit Learning (default) walks git history oldest-first, generating vague prompts from diffs and running N parallel agents (default 5) against parent commits, with state saved per-commit for resume; Prompt Mode runs a single prompt without git history. eli5.text: The tool now checks changes in reverse order to learn from past work, using multiple assistants at once for speed. It also cleans up leftover background tasks to prevent system slowdowns and reduces the amount of text it processes to save space.

facts: Use the shared Enter detector so the keypad Enter and the niche Linux terminals that send \n (linefeed) for Enter also commit; a raw name === 'return' check silently ignores those, which looks like a frozen menu (arrows move the highlight, Enter does nothing).
Recursively replace any lone (unpaired) UTF-16 surrogate with U+FFFD in every string reachable from `value`, mutating objects/arrays in place.

Sanitizing here, at the single chokepoint where all messages are converted to provider format, guarantees a single bad character can never poison the conversation regardless of which tool produced it. It is a no-op on already-valid strings, so valid emoji, base64, etc. are untouched.
Arrays and plain objects are both handled here: Object.keys enumerates array indices too, and indexing by string key mutates the element in place.

Neutralize any lone UTF-16 surrogates before the messages reach the provider. These are mutated in place; every aggregated message is a fresh clone (see convertToolMessage), so the caller's message history is unaffected.

This prevents strict server-side parsers (e.g., Rust serde_json) from rejecting entire request bodies due to corrupted history from unsafe truncation. Sanitization occurs at the message conversion chokepoint, mutating fresh clones to avoid affecting local history.

facts: Follow redirects manually so every hop is re-validated against the SSRF policy — a public URL must not be able to 30x its way to an internal one.
Normalize IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) so they are classified by their embedded IPv4 range rather than as generic IPv6.
Throws an {@link SsrfError} if the URL is not safe to fetch from the server: non-http(s) schemes, IP literals in a private/reserved range, or hostnames that resolve to such a range.

IP literals are always checked synchronously (no DNS needed). Hostname resolution is performed via `lookupHost` unless `resolveDns` is false — this lets callers that supply their own `fetch` (e.g. unit tests with stubbed responses) skip the network lookup while still rejecting literal addresses.

ai.summary: New ssrf.ts module enforces SSRF policies for read-url by validating URL schemes, IP literals, and resolved hostnames against private/reserved ranges. read-url.ts now follows redirects manually (max 5 hops) to re-validate each target, replacing native fetch redirect handling. IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) are normalized to their embedded IPv4 range for accurate classification. Callers can inject lookupHost or set resolveDns: false to skip DNS resolution while still blocking IP-literal targets.

facts: [Freebuff](https://www.npmjs.com/package/freebuff)** is the free, ad-supported version of Codebuff. No subscription. No credits. No configuration. Just install and start coding in your terminal.

What models do you use?** The best open-source models available. In full mode you can choose from DeepSeek V4 Pro, MiMo 2.5 Pro, Kimi K2.6, DeepSeek V4 Flash, MiMo 2.5, and MiniMax M3. Limited mode uses DeepSeek V4 Flash and MiMo 2.5. Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite handles file finding and research.

Which countries is Freebuff available in?** All countries. Freebuff runs in "full" mode in the US, Canada, UK, EU, and other select countries, and in "limited" mode everywhere else (or while using a VPN). See [freebuff.com](https://freebuff.com) for the full list.
What is limited mode?** Limited mode lets you use Freebuff outside the full-access countries, or while using a VPN. It includes DeepSeek V4 Flash and MiMo 2.5, with 5 one-hour sessions per day.
What data do you store?** We don't store your codebase. We only collect minimal logs for debugging purposes.

facts: Optional steering hook. Drained at each step boundary (after a step's LLM call + tools complete, before the next one). Any returned texts are appended to the message history as user prompts and keep the turn going, letting a host "steer" a running agent without aborting or losing the current step.

ai.title: SDK adds drainSteeringMessages hook for mid-turn agent steering
ai.summary: The SDK `RunOptions` type now accepts an optional `drainSteeringMessages` callback, allowing hosts to inject user messages into a running agent without aborting the current turn. In `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts`, this hook is drained at each step boundary after the LLM call and tool execution complete, appending returned texts to the message history as `USER_PROMPT` tagged messages. This mechanism ensures the agent responds to new inputs in the next step, maintaining a clean history state while extending the turn.

facts: Cap on how much of a failed stdio server's stderr we retain for the error message — enough to show the real failure without unbounded growth.
Buffer the child process's stderr so that a server which crashes during startup produces an actionable error instead of the opaque MCP SDK message "MCP error -32000: Connection closed".
When stderr is 'pipe' the SDK exposes a PassThrough immediately (before the process is spawned), so attaching here captures even early output from a child that dies during the connection handshake.

A failed MCP server (e.g. a stdio server that can't be spawned) should disable just its own tools, not abort the whole turn. The error from the client carries the actionable detail (command + captured stderr).

ai.title: Windows AVX2 detection via IsProcessorFeaturePresent with disk cache
ai.summary: CLI release scripts now detect Windows AVX2 support by invoking `IsProcessorFeaturePresent(40)` via PowerShell instead of relying solely on CPU model checks or assuming availability. Results are cached to disk to avoid repeated subprocess overhead on every launch, while Linux continues using `/proc/cpuinfo`. This change applies to `cli/release/index.js`, `cli/release-staging/index.js`, and `freebuff/cli/release/index.js`. Inconclusive probes (e.g., locked-down policies) default to assuming AVX2 for the current session without persisting the guess, relying on SIGILL fallbacks.

eli5.text: The program now checks your computer's ability to handle advanced math more accurately. This helps it run faster without guessing about your hardware.

ai.title: CLI session failure state carries retry timing and outcomeUnknown
ai.summary: The CLI's session state replaces the plain `error` string with a structured `FreebuffSessionFailure` type carrying `retry` timing and an `outcomeUnknown` flag. This distinguishes safe retries from potentially committed mutating requests, preventing duplicate takeover actions when the server may have processed a request before the client timed out. The `TakeoverPrompt` component now renders specific messages for 503, timeout, and unknown-outcome failures, with a countdown to the next retry. `classifyFreebuffSessionRequestFailure` encodes the policy: POST requests without a response are marked `outcomeUnknown` unless the server returns a documented 503 `service_overloaded`, while GET requests retry on 408, 429, and 5xx.

eli5.text: The app now tracks whether a request might have succeeded even if the screen timed out. This prevents it from accidentally repeating actions, like claiming a spot twice, when the connection drops.

facts: Split out of `ancillary`, because one shared budget wide enough for account_providers (75ms p50 on 2 round trips) was blind to lanes that actually run at 2-6ms. A budget that every lane passes is not a budget.

Still REPORTED, never paged — see the `breach` comment in evaluateDatabaseRequestCosts. Promoting these to pageable is a deliberate follow-up, and the precondition is a full week with every lane inside them.
The lane most worth driving down is `session_post`: 19 round trips at p95. With transport at ~11ms that is ~210ms of pure round-tripping, and round trips — not query time — are what handlers control.
One indexed read, on both services. The tightest lane we have, and the clearest read on transport cost: 1 round trip, so its p50 IS the floor.

The absolute budgets used to be unpageable for a hard reason: they were written against server execution time while this metric measures CLIENT wall time, so every lane sat 4-25x over them and paging made this alert red on every run for days — the same as no alert. That reason is gone.

facts: Machine-wide Git for Windows layouts. A per-user install (no admin rights) lands under %LOCALAPPDATA% instead, and is found via git.exe below.
The WSL launcher ships at C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe whether or not a distro is installed, so it must never be mistaken for a usable bash.

Where bash lives on a Windows machine. Every surface that needs a shell — the SDK's run_terminal_command, the Desktop terminal panel, the Desktop's per-workspace startup script — asks this module, so they can never disagree about whether this machine has bash.

Looking in enough places is the whole job. An install that we fail to find is indistinguishable to the user from no install at all: they run the installer, we keep saying bash is missing, and the only conclusion available to them is that the app is broken.

The installer's per-user mode, which is what a user without admin rights gets — and what an agent installing Git on the user's behalf gets, since it is not elevated either. This one is why "it installed Git and still says bash is missing" was reachable at all.

facts: The first version charged 1 / 2 / 3 / 5 and allowed a balance to run to -500. Measured a few days in: **17,993 of 18,013 accounts held a negative balance**, the median was -102, 2,125 were pinned at the floor, and 48 — forty-eight — had ever earned anything at all.

So it was not a slow tide. It was a meter that only ran one way, and what a user saw was a "Trust score" of -75 next to their name. People read that as an abuse finding and wrote in asking which fraud signal had flagged them, which is the worst possible reading of a currency meant to reward them.
Two things were wrong. The rates were too high for how much people actually send, and earning barely worked — the engagement feed was serving nothing, so the only reachable direction was down.

Free/standard models: DeepSeek Flash, MiMo, the web-standard pool. FREE — and `chargePromptTrust` returns early on a zero cost, so the overwhelming majority of prompts no longer write to the balance table or the ledger at all.

ai.title: Add HMAC-SHA256 account deletion proof utility
ai.summary: Added `createAccountDeletionProof` and `verifyAccountDeletionProof` in `common/src/util/account-deletion-proof.ts` to generate and validate server-side proofs for Adbuff deletion completion prior to Convex account purge. The proof is an HMAC-SHA256 signature over a versioned payload containing the identity subject and deletion code, ensuring integrity and preventing timing attacks via constant-time comparison. This mechanism binds the proof to both the authenticated subject and the mailed code, with the Next route minting it only after Adbuff reports an active suppression fence. The implementation enforces a minimum 32-character secret length and handles `Uint8Array` buffer compatibility for older TypeScript libraries.

eli5.text: The app now checks account deletion requests using a secure digital seal to prevent errors. This ensures your data is only removed after the request is fully verified.

facts: Markdown by default (same rendering as `/copy` via serializeConversation); a filename ending in `.json` exports the raw message objects instead, using the persistence-safe serializer so cyclic tool output can't throw.
Async on purpose: a multi-MB transcript flushed synchronously would block the CLI's render/input thread (the same reason writeFileAtomicAsync exists for the checkpoint writer).
Never clobber: the atomic write renames over the target, so an existing file — `/export README.md` from a slip or tab-complete — would be destroyed with no prompt and no backup.
Inside the try: a multi-MB transcript can throw from serialization itself (RangeError: Invalid string length), and that must surface as an ExportResult error rather than an unhandled rejection.

Previously `/export` was only an alias of `/copy` (32 KB OSC 52 clipboard cap); the alias is removed from `command-registry.ts` and `slash-commands.ts` so `/copy` keeps only `copy-chat`. `DEFAULT_CACHE_EXPIRY_MS` in `compact-history.ts` rises 30m -> 1h, and `agents/base3.ts` sets `compactContext: { cacheExpiryMs: 3600000 }` explicitly. `run-agent-step.ts` now gates the history-replacing branch on `isCompactCommandPrompt` (same map that injects `compactPrompt`) and skips compaction when the model returns empty or think-only text, preventing total amnesia.

facts: Whether the demand attached third-party measurement, and in which channel. Without this we cannot tell "the partner sent no trackers" from "we dropped them", which is exactly the question that gets asked when an advertiser reports missing impressions.
Third-party measurement attached by the demand partners funding an Imprezia ad, delivered from the end user's device.

Delivering it is not optional. These pixels and frames belong to the advertiser's own measurement vendor, not to Imprezia: an ad whose trackers never fire is one the advertiser never counts as delivered, however correctly we report it on our own beacon.
This has to run on the END USER'S device. Firing these server-side would carry a datacenter IP and a server UA and be discounted as invalid traffic, which is the same as not delivering them at all.
Hygiene on a long-lived page: drop the frame once it has loaded.

ai.title: readfiles attaches images as media parts via requestImageFile
ai.summary: read_files now returns image files as base64 media parts instead of text, allowing the model to see the picture. This requires hosts to provide the new optional `requestImageFile` dependency in `AgentRuntimeScopedDeps`; without it, images fall back to the old text-read behavior which produces replacement characters. The SDK implements this for local filesystems in `sdk/src/tools/read-files.ts` and wires it through `sdk/src/run.ts`, while `common/src/tools/params/tool/read-files.ts` updates the output schema to accept media objects. Images exceeding `MAX_IMAGE_READ_BYTES` (derived from `MAX_IMAGE_BASE64_SIZE`) are rejected with a status line instructing the model to downscale them via terminal commands.

ai.title: fitToolResults preserves fresh tool exchanges during history
ai.summary: Added fitToolResults utility to agent-runtime to prevent truncation of unconsumed tool batches during history compaction. The compaction logic now reserves the latest assistant/tool exchange and calculates fixed token overhead (system prompt, schemas, next step) before summarizing older history. This ensures large fresh reads do not squeeze the active task out of the BYOK window, covering core agent loop and request budgeting.

eli5.text: The assistant now keeps its most recent actions and results intact while shortening older parts of the conversation. This helps prevent it from forgetting what it just did, making responses more accurate and consistent.

facts: A successful no-op is not progress. GLM can keep emitting the same to-do list (even while acknowledging the loop in prose) until the general step budget is exhausted. Give it a chance to recover, then fail explicitly.

Count identical completed to-do calls at the tail of this user turn. Prose/reasoning and per-step scaffolding are not progress. A different list, another tool, or a user message is. Only matched, completed calls count, so interrupted/failed tool execution cannot masquerade as this model loop.
Compare task/status rather than object key order or provider call IDs.

entries.summary: New files: `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/todo-loop.ts`.

ai.title: Todo-loop detection added to agent runtime
ai.summary: Added `trailingIdenticalTodoCalls` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/todo-loop.ts` to detect GLM models repeating identical `write_todos` calls without progress. `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` injects a recovery message at 3 consecutive loops and throws `TodoLoopError` at 6, stopping the turn explicitly. Detection compares task/status pairs, ignoring key order and provider call IDs, while skipping scaffolding and recovery messages.

eli5.text: The assistant now detects when it gets stuck in a loop of repeating the same task updates. It automatically tries to fix this behavior, and if that fails, it stops the response to prevent endless repetition.

ai.title: Add allowInferenceSourceChange flag to run options
ai.summary: Added `allowInferenceSourceChange` flag to `RunOptions` in `sdk/src/run.ts` to permit explicit history transfer between inference sources. Default behavior preserves strict source pinning; provider failures never authorize transfer, only user-selected connections can trigger it. Scope covers SDK core (`run.ts`, `client.ts`) and BYOK error messaging (`byok.ts`). The flag ensures returned state and checkpoints pin the new source for subsequent runs.

eli5.text: You can now choose to switch the assistant's underlying model during a conversation. This keeps your chat history, but the assistant will use the new model for future replies.
